{{Top|leg}}
{{Quote|Some historians believe Darth is a contraction of ''dark'' and ''Sith'', while others suggest it was a corruption of ''daritha'', an ancient Rakatan word for 'emperor.' In any event, the honorific Darth was introduced to the Sith Lords.|Darth Sidious teaches Maul the history of the Sith|<ref name="The Wrath of Darth Maul">''[[The Wrath of Darth Maul]]''</ref>}}
'''Daritha''' was a [[Rakata (language)|Rakatan]] word that meant [[Emperor/Legends|emperor]]. Some [[Historian/Legends|historians]] believed that the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] title [[Darth/Legends|''Darth'']] stemmed from this word.<ref name="JvS>[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> The [[Cronese]] language adopted the word<ref name="Xim Week Part I">{{Hyperspace|url=fans/hyperspace/source/ximweek02/index.html|text=Xim Week: ''The Despotica'' (Part I)|int=Xim Week: The Despotica}}</ref> after the fall of the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakatan]] [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]],<ref name="Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> and Daritha came to mean ''Ruler of Worlds.''   It was taken as a title by the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Xim/Legends|Xim the Despot]].<ref name="Xim Week">{{SW|url=news/essential-atlas-extra-the-history-of-xim-and-the-tion-cluster|text=Essential Atlas Extra: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster|int=Xim Week: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster}}</ref>
